correction.distinguish_from_the_region_rescue: The region-repair rescue embedded authorization in-payload and its launcher accepts that, so it is consistent there. This contract's validator requires the external form. The lesson is to use the mechanism the launch path actually reads, not the one used last time.
correction.resolution: Contracts restored byte-for-byte to the authorized payloads and verified to recompute to d7d2fbc2 and 4486c376 with no authorization block and status back to prepared. This receipt stays EXTERNAL and is passed to the launcher via its intended --authorization-payload-sha256 argument.
correction.the_rule: SCIENTIFIC PAYLOAD IS NOT AUTHORIZATION METADATA. Authorization POINTS AT an immutable payload by hash; it must never become part of it. Recording consent must not change the bytes that were consented to.
correction.what_i_did_wrong: I recorded authorization by INSERTING an `authorization` block and flipping `status` INSIDE the scientific payload. That mutated the payload and moved its hash off the value the owner had authorized (d7d2fbc2 -> d74a6f5d, 4486c376 -> 4863298b), so the launcher was then being asked to accept a contract nobody had authorized.

supersedes.reason: The v1 wrapper validated against the superseded v1 contract module AND required an authorized status INSIDE the scientific payload. Repairing it necessarily changes modal_apps/t4_5ht1b2_protonation_rescue_<arm>_app.py, which is pinned inside runtime_inputs_sha256, which is inside the payload -- so the contract identity had to move. A launcher cannot be repaired while keeping the run identity it pins.
